name: RWANDA

flag.title: Flag of Rwanda
flag.note: Blue, yellow & green with a gold sun

lead: Rwanda is a tiny landlocked country in the heart of Africa, so packed with steep green hills it earned the name "Land of a Thousand Hills." Once torn apart by tragedy in 1994, it rebuilt itself into one of Africa's cleanest, safest nations — and the place where women hold more seats in parliament than anywhere else on Earth.
geo: Rwanda sits high above sea level — even its lowest valleys are about 1,000 m up. The whole country is crumpled into ridge after ridge of emerald hills, with river valleys draining into both the Congo and Nile basins.

In the north, the Virunga Volcanoes rear up like sleeping giants wrapped in cloud-forest. Lake Kivu gleams along the western border, while Nyungwe Forest in the south is one of Africa's oldest rainforests.
animals: Rwanda's star animal is the mountain gorilla — a gentle giant living only in the Virunga and Bwindi forests. Fewer than 1,000 survive in the wild, and Rwanda protects roughly a third of them inside Volcanoes National Park.

Nyungwe Forest shelters chimpanzees and black-and-white colobus monkeys that leap between treetops in dramatic flashes. Over 700 bird species have been recorded across the country — a birdwatcher's paradise.
culture: Rwandans celebrate Umuganura, a harvest festival, every August. Music and dance are central: the intore dance features warriors leaping dramatically in headdresses made of white sisal fibres that stream like waterfalls.

Basket-weaving is a national art — tightly coiled peace baskets (agaseke) hang in galleries worldwide. Every last Saturday of the month is Umuganda, community work day, when everyone sweeps streets and plants trees together.
history: For centuries Rwanda was a powerful kingdom ruled by a mwami (king), famed for its organised army and cattle-rich culture. Belgian colonisers drew sharp ethnic divisions that planted seeds of terrible conflict.

In 1994, around 800,000 people were killed in just 100 days. But Rwandans chose reconciliation — community courts called gacaca heard over a million cases, and the country rebuilt with extraordinary speed and unity.
wows: Rwanda's parliament is over 60% female — the highest proportion of any parliament in the world.
Kigali is rated Africa's cleanest city; plastic bags have been banned since 2008.
A single gorilla trek permit costs 1,500 USD — gorillas are Rwanda's top tourist earner.
Rwanda has no straight roads longer than about 30 km because the hills never stop.
Rwandans hold a communal work day every month; even the president picks up a shovel.
Lake Kivu sits on a vast pocket of dissolved methane Rwanda is piping up for electricity.
Despite being landlocked, Rwanda has a national sailing team that competes internationally.

myths.myth: Rwanda is still dangerous and war-torn
myths.fact: Rwanda is now one of Africa's safest countries — Kigali's streets are cleaner and safer than many European capitals, and tourist numbers hit record highs every year.

myths.myth: Gorillas are aggressive and attack people
myths.fact: Mountain gorillas are shy and peaceful; habituated groups in Volcanoes Park largely ignore visitors, and no tourist has ever been seriously harmed on a trek.
